top3.headline: Experts sided with Claude's hidden lean on 86% of judgment calls
top3.whyItMatters: Agent-assisted decisions can carry the agent's lean while people believe the call was theirs.

top3.headline: Claude Opus 5.5 tops a harder, mostly private AI benchmark
top3.whyItMatters: Cost per task varies more than 13x among top models, so price belongs in model choices.

top3.headline: A state machine stopped agents changing bookings without customer consent
top3.whyItMatters: Hard limits on agent actions caught violations the benchmark's own scoring missed.

items.title: T3 Code's triage command hands bugs to your own agent
items.takeaway: The cmd+k command clones the source for your exact version, gives your agent a playbook, and files an issue if the bug is T3 Code's.
items.soWhat: Tools can now ship playbooks so customers' own agents debug them and file issues.

items.title: Artificial Analysis Index v5: Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 58
items.takeaway: 60% of the index now uses private or held-out tests; the open-weights gap widened from 3 to 12 points.
items.soWhat: Cost per task varies more than 13x among top models, so price belongs in every model choice.

items.title: Concordat stopped agents from making unconfirmed changes on airline tasks
items.takeaway: Standard agents changed bookings without a required yes in up to 13 of 50 tasks; Concordat agents made none.
items.soWhat: Enforcing allowed actions in code, not prompts, blocked risky agent moves without hurting task success.

image.alt: arXiv: Concordat stopped agents from making unconfirmed changes on airline tasks

items.title: Coding agents' success falls from 63% to 29% as features evolve
items.takeaway: Across 10 agents and 73 tasks, inherited defects appeared in 72.9% of failed later stages.
items.soWhat: Long agent sessions compound hidden defects, so test the whole feature, not just the latest change.

image.alt: arXiv: Coding agents' success falls from 63% to 29% as features evolve

items.title: AI agent swarms formalized a 15,000-page math proof in 24 days
items.takeaway: Axiom Math produced about 43.1 million lines of Lean and found 34 noteworthy deviations from the published record.
items.soWhat: Agent swarms can now check massive expert work and surface deviations humans published and missed.

related.name: Axiom blog: Formalizing the Enormous Theorem

items.title: Spine cut a coding agent's cost 32% while raising its score
items.takeaway: Built into Codex, it raised SWE-Milestone score 11.8%; it matched subagent delegation at 73.7% lower cost.
items.soWhat: Better context management made the agent both cheaper and better, not a tradeoff between them.

image.alt: arXiv: Spine cut a coding agent's cost 32% while raising its score

items.title: Automatic skill optimizers added tokens but no real accuracy gains
items.takeaway: Learned skills scored +0.1 points over the hand-written seed on average while reading about 16% more input tokens.
items.soWhat: Test any auto-tuned agent instructions on held-out tasks before trusting reported gains.

items.title: Analysts followed a coding agent's hidden lean 86% of the time
items.takeaway: In Anthropic's study of 50 analysts, only 15% credited the agent; Anthropic says real-world relevance is unknown.
items.soWhat: Experts using agents may adopt the agent's judgment as their own; check who really decided.
